summary: The component catalog is generated from exported React components under src/ui and selected helpers under src/ui/_shared. Its two tables report source file, signature, optional documentation and styles. Reuse a catalog entry before creating another control; behavior remains owned by the component source and reference/ui. Current extension-related entries include the package manager, bounded guest renderer, settings editor, effect-review surface, and Library/Workbench host-command menu. The command menu reuses the shared virtual-row primitive to bound mounted options while keeping keyboard navigation and an in-flight command reachable. ScenePage also exposes the identifiers used for verified navigation handoff. The catalog is discovery metadata, not a behavior registry or release proof. PromptEditPanel and PhaseEditor signatures include the shared staged attachment lifecycle so preset and Promptbook block controls reuse the same file authoring surface. Table Read contributes its discovered room, Setup, Conversation, InterviewScene, ReaderPicker and LivingCard exports; CharacterTextControl shares actual text/prose controls with the Workbench; ReaderPicker selects cosmetic artwork through existing preferences.

sections.title: Use this for
sections.summary: A short table answers the common UI needs before anyone searches the full catalog. Any action with text uses the Button from the button family, with one primary per view, danger for destructive actions and quiet for low emphasis. An icon-only action is an IconButton with a label; a few options are a Segmented; sections of a room or editor are Tabs; a small on/off filter or tag is a Chip; a clickable row is a ListRow, a menu entry a MenuItem, a fold a Disclosure, a small square target a Tile, a larger face a Card, a tiny mark a Dot. It also names the icon door Ic, SwatchRow and PaintPicker for colors, Toggle for switches, InkDialog or DialogCore for dialogs, and the three theme font tokens. For buttons, color pickers and fonts, lint and the style guard block the alternatives; the rest is the house answer that review checks.

sections.title: Components (React, `.tsx`)
sections.summary: The React table lists exported components from the shell, Library, Workbench, Scenes, Settings and shared UI. Extension entries include the manager, guest renderer, settings editor, effect-review panel and host-command menu used in Library and Workbench. The menu uses the existing virtual-row primitive for a bounded DOM window and retains keyboard access to commands. ScenePage exposes navigation-ticket and load identifiers for verified handoff. Scene layout entries include AdditionalLayout, Desktop98, FullChatWings and Storybook; ChatLayoutRow records its .grid style. Rows are generated discovery metadata; consult reference/ui and component source for behavior. Other entries include shared controls, editors, panels and app-specific surfaces. The generated PromptEditPanel and PhaseEditor entries include attachment uploads and their shared staging lifecycle; signatures are discovery metadata rather than independent feature promises. Table Read contributes its discovered room, Setup, Conversation, InterviewScene, ReaderPicker and LivingCard exports; CharacterTextControl shares actual text/prose controls with the Workbench; ReaderPicker selects cosmetic artwork through existing preferences.

sections.title: Shared UI helpers (`src/ui/_shared`, `.ts`)
sections.summary: Secondary table for exported TypeScript UI helpers under src/ui/_shared whose names begin create, build, swatch, or inject. These are ordinary `.ts` functions rather than JSX components; the table makes no deprecation or migration claim. It uses the same Name, File, Signature, Doc, and Styles columns as the React table. Current entries are buildTimeline from version-history, a pure helper the Updates surface uses to derive release relations and behind counts, and createArtCache, the bounded in-memory art cache that dedupes decrypted portraits and revokes its object URLs on eviction or clear (the app's singleton is also cleared on library lock). Regenerating the catalog adds or removes rows as matching exports change. Open this table when a UI task needs shared computation or construction logic, and open the React table when it needs a rendered control.
